name: Pidilite Industries Ltd.
business_summary: India's leading adhesives and construction-chemicals company (Fevicol, Fevikwik, M-Seal, Dr. Fixit, Araldite, Roff, Fevicryl, Motomax). Consumer & Bazaar (C&B) ~80% of sales, Business-to-Business (B2B: industrial adhesives, pigments, resins) ~21%; international subsidiaries ~14% of revenue. Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 4,298 cr (+20.9%) on UVG of 11.1% (C&B) and 9.2% (B2B), but gross margin collapsed to 48.6% (from 55%) and EBITDA margin to 20.4% (24%), at the bottom of the 20-24% corridor; PAT Rs 626 cr (+7.2%). Price hikes of 12-15% in Q1 and 3-5% in October are rebuilding margin; management guides H2 margin at the higher end of 20-24%. Almost debt free, 69% promoter-held, 59x trailing P/E.

revenue_mix.segment: Consumer & Bazaar (adhesives, sealants, construction chemicals, DIY, art & craft)

exposures.mechanism: Petrochemical-derived raw materials (VAM, acrylic monomers, epoxy, solvents, resins) are ~44% of sales (COGS 51.4% of sales in Q2 x ~85%). +10% Brent -> RM +4% -> +1.8% of sales; Pidilite recovers ~70% through price hikes within 1-2 quarters (12-15% in Q1, 3-5% in Oct), leaving 0.55% of sales unrecovered vs EBITDA margin 22% -> EBITDA -2.5%; EV/MCap 0.99; persistence 0.25 plus a margin-guidance/multiple effect on a 59x stock -> -1.0. Matches empirical -0.96 (t -3.1) and F_REFINING_MARGIN -0.71 (t -2.5). This edge already contains the feedstock channel; do not add F_CHEM_FEEDSTOCK separately for the same Brent shock.

evidence.note: Gross margin 48.6% vs 55% (-640 bp) on material inflation; EBITDA margin 20.4% vs 24%
MD flags sustained crude above $100/bbl as key risk; Q2 margin near lower end of 20-24% band

exposures.mechanism: Idiosyncratic feedstock moves not driven by Brent: VAM spiked to nearly US$2,000/t before cooling to ~US$1,000 (West Asia supply). +10% feedstock (benzene/propylene/VAM basket) at ~44% of sales -> +4.4% of sales; 75% recovered -> 1.1% of sales vs 22% margin -> EBITDA -5%; x0.99 x persistence 0.25 -> -1.2. Use only for feedstock shocks orthogonal to Brent (supply outages, China export curbs).

evidence.note: VAM spiked to nearly $2,000 then cooled to ~$1,000; doubling input costs needs 2x price to hold gross margin %

exposures.mechanism: Imported raw materials ~30% of RM (VAM, epoxy, TiO2, pigments) ~15% of sales; international subsidiaries (~14% of revenue, EBITDA +53% in Q2) give a partial translation offset. +3% USD/INR -> +0.46% of sales cost, 60% recovered -> 0.18% /22% = EBITDA -0.8%; subs translation +0.35% EBITDA; net small (-0.2 fundamental). Empirical -2.32 (t -2.7) and DXY -1.65 (t -2.9) are larger because INR weakness coincides with foreign outflows from premium-multiple FMCG-like names; shrink halfway -> -1.0.

Fevicol (carpentry/furniture), Dr. Fixit/construction chemicals, tile adhesives and Roff are tied to housing and interiors, ~50% of revenue. +10% residential volumes -> +3% sales growth on that half = +1.5% revenue; EBITDA +2.1% (leverage 1.4x); EV/MCap 0.99; persistence 0.5 -> +1.0; growth-multiple support (59x) -> +1.5.

Premium/DIY and consumer adhesives (Fevikwik, M-Seal, hobby) are urban-skewed. +5 pp urban discretionary growth -> UVG +1.5 pp -> revenue +1.5%; EBITDA +2.4%; persistence 0.5 -> +1.2; 59x trailing multiple doubles the sensitivity to growth -> +2.5.

evidence.note: Sustained double-digit UVG for 6-8 consecutive quarters

exposures.mechanism: Bazaar/rural distribution ~35% of C&B volumes. +5 pp rural growth -> UVG +0.8 pp -> revenue +0.8%; EBITDA +1.2%; x0.99 x 0.5 plus multiple -> +1.2.

evidence.note: Broad-based double-digit volume growth in Consumer & Bazaar

exposures.mechanism: Almost debt free (interest Rs 53 cr TTM), so only a discount-rate/housing-demand channel. At 59x trailing earnings the multiple duration is ~25 years; +25 bp repo -> ~+10 bp on long yields -> ~-2.5% before offsets -> -1.5 after demand offset.
Packaging ~7% of costs (estimate); +10% -> +0.6% of cost, 75% recovered -> EBITDA -0.5%; x0.99 x 0.25 -> -0.1; widened for plastics-linked correlation with crude -> -0.5.

evidence.note: Cost of goods Rs 2,211 cr vs Rs 1,598 cr y/y (+38%)

exposures.mechanism: Lower GST on construction/consumer items (adhesives, paints) lowers shelf price: +3 pp cut x elasticity 0.7 -> volume +2%; Pidilite also benefits from branded vs unorganised formalisation; revenue-neutral on price, EBITDA +2.5% -> +1.5.

evidence.note: Management confident of continuing H1 momentum into H2

exposures.mechanism: Direct effects beyond crude: MENA subsidiary revenue hit by working-capital constraints, India-to-West-Asia exports underperforming, VAM/solvent supply disruption. MENA+West Asia exports est. ~4% of revenue; -25% -> -1% revenue, 100% drop-through at 12-15% EBIT -> -4% EBITDA; x0.99 x 0.4 -> -1.6.

evidence.note: MENA business revenue headwinds; exports to West Asia underperforming on ongoing conflicts

exposures.mechanism: Value-added launches (Multilock, Expert, Wonderlock, Araldite Wood) and mix to premium sustain 22-24% margins in normal input costs. +1 = premium share +2 pp -> gross margin +60 bp -> EBITDA +3%; persistence 0.6 x 0.99 -> +1.8 -> +2.

evidence.note: New products Multilock, Expert, Wonderlock, Araldite Wood; AI-led distribution

exposures.mechanism: Cheaper Chinese epoxy, acrylic and solvent exports lower Pidilite's input prices and add competition from imported adhesives; net positive on RM (+15% export intensity -> RM -1.5% -> EBITDA +2%; persistence 0.25) -> +0.6.

evidence.note: China chemical export intensity and Indian RM sourcing; not verified for Pidilite specifically

supply_chain.counterparty: VAM, acrylic, epoxy, solvent and pigment suppliers (global petrochemicals, West Asia)
Hardware, paint and building-material dealers (~dealer network of lakhs)
supply_chain.note: Bazaar channel; rebates passed to trade as RM eases

Further selective price cuts / rebates as VAM and other raw materials ease
CFO transition: Amit Agarwal appointed CFO-designate

current_state.latest_quarter: Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026), reported 2026-10-28: revenue Rs 4,298 cr (+20.9%), EBITDA Rs 877 cr (+3.1%; 20.4%), PAT Rs 626 cr (+7.2%); gross margin 48.6%; UVG C&B 11.1%, B2B 9.2%; Q1 EBITDA margin was ~26%
